issue_context.title: Relative Volume (RVOL) Indicator
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Support "Relative Volume (RVOL)" Indicator
https://www.smbtraining.com/blog/relative-volume-rvol-defined-and-how-we-use-it

#### Actual Behavior
No implementation of "Relative Volume (RVOL)" indicator

#### Potential Solution
Implement "Relative Volume (RVOL)" Indicator

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
comments: I believe Jovad implemented this indicator already, no?
Believe your right @ikamanu, thank you for catching this 👍. Duplicate https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues/5746 and PR implementation https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/pull/5747

review_comments:
This could be an `IndicatorBase<TradeBar>` instead of a `WindowIndicator`, since you are already using a `Sum` indicator to track the volume sum in the period and also that would mean the indicator won't hold the window of samples twice.

You could even replace the `Sum` indicator with a `SimpleMovingAverage` directly to track the volume average instead of calculating it yourself. This way we avoid duplication and keep it as simple as possible!

These tests could be quite simple, just let `CommonIndicatorTests` do the heavy lifting for you! 😁 

You just have to set the file name and the RVOL column name (as you did) and `CommonIndicatorTests` will run a test suite for your indicator, including warm up period, reseting and asserting that the calculated values are what is expected from the `TestColumnName` column, so the `Assertion`, `ResetsProperly` and `WarmsUpProperly` are not necessary in this case, `CommonIndicatorTests` asserts that perfectly!

Also, from what I can see in the dataset, the indicator's period should be 20.
Usually in Lean constructors are placed at the top, after attributes and properties, and before any other methods.
You can make this constructor have the same default 'period' value as the one bellow 👌  `int period = 50`
You could type it directly as `Sum` (or the moving average indicator you could use), given that it won't be of any other type and it would also be clearer.
